output.brief: The rise in VA-220 failures comes from the Pellacott valves, not from the new installers or firmware 4.2. The lab matched claims by serial number. Pellacott 2026 valves fail at the same rate (about 41 per 1,000) across legacy and new installers and across both firmware versions. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7 per 1,000 in every group. Unused Pellacott 2026 warehouse valves leak at the seat in 11% of cases, against 0–1% for others. The calibration contractor found that Pellacott's only VA-220 leak rig has been out of service since January 2026. No VA-220 test program is loaded on the other rigs, and the 2026 certificates repeat value sequences from 2025. The certificates therefore appear not to reflect real tests, and the score jump came from complete-looking records, not better product. Do not release the six held lots on new certificates. Quarantine all 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and release stock only after Brenmoor runs its own helium tests. Drop the installer remediation and chargeback plan. Secure dual-source supply to avoid the line stoppage. The seal change and the new line are suspects, but they can't be separated yet, so don't order a seal reversal until that is tested. Verify the other suppliers' test records, since their conformance scores also jumped. Fix the scoring so credit needs rig logs or witnessed tests.
